Caption: 

# **Thursday links**

[Another chance for dinner with the President](https://gettrumpmemes.com/leaderboards?experience=trump-dinner&page=4)

Some good news on inflation: the cost of attending “the most exclusive dinner in the world” is falling fast.

In May of last year, you needed approximately $380,000 worth of the TRUMP memecoin to rank among the 220 holders who qualified for a dinner with the President. Entry to the VIP reception required roughly $5 million worth.

This was a bargain!

For comparison, a Super PAC once [sold tickets](https://www.wired.com/story/people-paying-millions-donald-trump-mar-a-lago/?utm_source=chatgpt.com) to a “candlelight dinner” with the president for _$1 million_ each. Donors were also offered a one-on-one meeting with the president for $5 million.

It’s an even bigger bargain now. Another dinner with TRUMP holders is scheduled for November and it looks dramatically easier to get an invite. 

The event is a little more exclusive, with only 185 guests making the cut this time. But cheaper. Right now, the 100th registrant holds just 404 TRUMP, which is worth just $730 these days.

The 29th registrant — the last currently qualified for the VIP reception — holds 9,300 TRUMP, worth about $14,000.

In other words, the cost of attending the most exclusive dinner in the world appears to have fallen by at least 99.8% in about a year and a half.

Plus, you can sell your tokens immediately after the qualification window closes and get most of your money back!

Honestly, I might try it.

[Mathpocalypse now?](https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10169')

Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson captured the mixed feelings elicited by OpenAI’s [release](https://openai.com/index/sharing-ai-progress-in-mathematics/) of 377 new results in mathematics yesterday. He [describes](https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10169') it as “one of the biggest days in mathematical history” — but also a “mathpocalypse.” 

(Note: Aaronson is real. It’s the computer science he studies that’s theoretical.)

80503.body:
QCP forecasts $80,000 to $90,000 Q4 range for bitcoin | Samsung to bring USDC transfers on Solana to U.S. Galaxy users | Vitalik Buterin warns against rushing wallet migrations over AI risks | JPMorgan estimates $50 billion in crypto inflows this year as Q4 momentum improves | TD Cowen says dilution could limit Strategy shareholder gains despite higher bitcoin forecasts

The Daily ( https://www.theblock.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Written by Yogita Khatri | Edited by Kyle Baird

Presented By:

( https://polymarket.us/?deep_link_sub1=THEBLOCK&c=NEWSLETTER&shortlink=94gey3fp&source_caller=api_v2&onelink_id=S8ac&pid=THEBLOCK&deep_link_value=midterms&utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

Happy Thursday! *Bitcoin* continues to trade lower, now around *$81,700* , with analysts forecasting a trading range of *$80,000 to $90,000* for the fourth quarter.

Also in today's newsletter, *Samsung* plans to launch USDC transfers on Solana for U.S. Galaxy users, *Vitalik Buterin* warns against rushing wallet migrations over growing AI threats, *JPMorgan* estimates *$50 billion* has flowed into crypto this year, and more.

Meanwhile, the crypto industry is split ( https://www.theblock.co/news/defi/2026-10-08-crypto-industry-split-over-justin-drakes-ai-warning-418021?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) over *Justin Drake* 's private key recovery warning, and *South Korea* ranks ( https://www.theblock.co/research/institutional/block-gcci-2026-country-profile-korea-crypto-market-418081?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) 12th out of 15 countries in The Block's 2026 Global Crypto Competitiveness Index.

P.S. Don't forget to check out The Latent ( https://thelatent.co/?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) , our sister website covering AI. Get The Latent Daily here ( https://thelatent.co/newsletter?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ) and all other The Block newsletters here ( https://www.theblock.co/newsletters?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters ).

*THE BIG ONE*

*🟠 Bitcoin pulls back as QCP forecasts $80,000-90,000 Q4 range*

( https://www.theblock.co/news/markets/2026-10-08-bitcoin-q4-forecast-418052?utm_campaign=website&utm_medium=referral&utm_source=theblocknewsletters )

*Bitcoin fell below $82,000* on Thursday after topping $87,000 last Friday, while *QCP Capital* expects the cryptocurrency to trade *between $80,000 and $90,000* in its base case for the fourth quarter.

* QCP sees *$80,000 to $82,000 as an area to buy* bitcoin and would *reduce exposure around $88,000 to $90,000* if ETF inflows fail to pick up.
* The firm's *bull case puts bitcoin above $100,000* , supported by stronger ETF inflows, stablecoin growth, a Fed pause, a softer dollar, lower real yields
